factual_and_methodological.summary: ECB primary sources confirm the September 10, 2026 increase of the deposit, MRO and marginal lending rates to 2.50%, 2.65% and 2.90%; the 2025 TARGET figures; and the September 21, 2026 launch of Pontes for wholesale tokenised-asset settlement in central-bank money. The dossier distinguishes Eurosystem monetary authority, national implementation and the separate legal roles surrounding tokenised assets.

editorial_publication_readiness.opening: Direct mechanism-led opening; no generic sophistication claims or product-process narration.
editorial_publication_readiness.headings: Headings advance the actor-specific mechanism, constraints, contrary evidence and revision conditions.
editorial_publication_readiness.language_localization: EN and PT-BR are semantically aligned; PT-BR technical prose was localized before approval.
editorial_publication_readiness.cohesion: Argument moves from rights/capability through transmission, constraints and evidence that would revise the assessment.
editorial_publication_readiness.template_meta_qa: No prompt, QA-process, schema, renderer or roadmap leakage detected.

contextual_depth.summary: The dossier distinguishes legal rights, operating capability, transmission, substitutability and institutional constraints rather than relying on scale or reputation.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: At least two analytical tables, one quantitative chart, one causal flow and one mind map in both locales.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: Visuals encode sourced quantities or mechanisms defended in prose and are not combined into a synthetic power score.

contrary_evidence: A common policy rate does not produce identical borrowing conditions across heterogeneous national banking and sovereign markets.
Pontes is operationally new; launch alone does not establish large market adoption or displacement of alternative settlement arrangements.
limitations: Future structural relevance of Pontes depends on actual participation, volume, interoperability and legal integration.
Settlement infrastructure supports finality but does not determine the commercial merits or ownership of the underlying transaction.
notes: Dedicated single-actor Strategic Actors dossier. Primary-source factual core, controlled taxonomy, bilingual parity and visual evidence reviewed; no public bundle for this ID at approval time.

en.title: Eurosystem: a shared monetary authority with distributed implementation and settlement infrastructure
en.deck: The Eurosystem combines common euro-area monetary decisions with distributed implementation through national central banks and shared settlement infrastructure. Pontes now extends central-bank money into tokenised wholesale settlement.
en.regime: Common euro-area monetary authority operates through distributed central-bank implementation and increasingly integrated settlement infrastructure.
en.key_risk: Conflating the Eurosystem with all EU institutions or assuming a common policy produces identical national transmission obscures institutional boundaries.

pt-BR.title: Eurosistema: autoridade monetária compartilhada, implementação distribuída e infraestrutura de liquidação
pt-BR.deck: O Eurosistema combina decisões monetárias comuns da área do euro com implementação distribuída pelos bancos centrais nacionais e infraestrutura compartilhada. O Pontes agora estende moeda de banco central à liquidação atacadista tokenizada.
pt-BR.regime: Autoridade monetária comum opera por implementação distribuída dos bancos centrais e infraestrutura de liquidação cada vez mais integrada.
pt-BR.key_risk: Confundir o Eurosistema com todas as instituições da UE ou presumir transmissão nacional idêntica esconde limites institucionais.

publication.selection_rationale: The Eurosystem is an active Strategic Actors record with a documented global-financing and settlement-infrastructure channel but lacked a dedicated single-actor canonical study.
